stem: Regarding the trochlear nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The trochlear nerve has both sensory and motor function.
The trochlear nerve innervates the superior rectus muscle.
The trochlear nerve has the shortest intracranial course.
The trochlear nerve enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure.
Trochlear nerve palsy results in loss of eyeball adduction.
fact: CN IV is purely motor, supplies superior oblique, has the longest intracranial course, and enters via the superior orbital fissure.
finding: NCBI supports the trochlear course and orbital entry.

stem: A 55 year old woman presents to ED complaining of vertical diplopia with difficulty walking downstairs. She is tilting her head to one side as she says this helps ease the diplopia. Which of the following extraocular muscles is responsible for this picture:
fact: Superior oblique dysfunction causes vertical diplopia and difficulty walking downstairs.

stem: The lingual nerve supplies which of the following:
options: Taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue
Sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue
Sensation from the upper teeth and associated gingiva
fact: The lingual nerve carries general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.

stem: A patient presents with spontaneous onset of left sided facial weakness but is otherwise well. He is unable to purse his lips, close his eye fully or raise his eyebrow on the left side, which of the following is the most likely cause:
fact: Bell palsy is the common isolated lower-motor-neuron facial palsy and involves the forehead and eye closure.
mnemonic: LMN VII affects the whole side.
finding: NCBI supports isolated peripheral facial palsy features.

stem: The glossopharyngeal nerve supplies general sensation to all of the following regions EXCEPT for:
fact: Upper teeth and associated gingiva are supplied by V2, not CN IX.
mnemonic: IX covers posterior tongue and throat; V2 covers upper teeth.
finding: NCBI supports CN IX sensory territories and excludes upper teeth.

stem: A 21 year old female presents to ED with isolated facial nerve palsy. You diagnose Bell's palsy. Which of the following clinical features might you expect on examination:
options: Sensory loss over the cornea and conjunctiva
Loss of the corneal blink reflex
Loss of sensation over the ipsilateral face
fact: CN VII is the efferent corneal-blink limb through orbicularis oculi.
finding: Facial palsy can abolish the efferent corneal blink response.

stem: The facial nerve exits the skull through the:
fact: CN VII exits the facial canal and skull through the stylomastoid foramen.
mnemonic: VII exits between styloid and mastoid.

stem: Which of the following nerves is the efferent pathway of the gag reflex:
fact: CN X is the efferent gag-reflex limb; CN IX is afferent.
finding: NCBI supports vagal efferent gag function.

stem: The oculomotor nerve supplies all of the following structures EXCEPT for the:
fact: Superior oblique is supplied by CN IV; CN III supplies the other listed structures.
finding: NCBI supports the CN III muscle and parasympathetic distribution.

stem: A 28 year old man presents to ED complaining of severe headaches and dizziness. Imaging shows a tumour compressing the hypoglossal canal. Which of the following clinical features would you most expect to see:
options: Uvula deviation away from affected side
Tongue deviation on protrusion towards affected side
fact: CN XII injury causes ipsilateral tongue weakness and deviation toward the affected side on protrusion.
mnemonic: XII points the tongue toward the lesion.
